P0_timing_boundary_source_review.conclusion: P1/P3 acquisition timing boundary is comparable to the canonical P0 materialization reference.

claim_boundaries: 231.6382 ms is a frozen canonical P0 reference observation, not an estimate of the P0 population median. Candidate PASS means lower median acquisition than this canonical reference under the frozen protocol; it does not establish general statistical superiority over all possible P0 runs.
P3 COLD_UNBUFFERED refers only to the frozen cache-bypassing Windows I/O path; it must not be generalized to universal cold-storage performance.
P1 serialized acquisition excludes any future overlap benefit. Any overlap study must be separately preregistered after this experiment.
A/B steady-state latency and EXEC148 residency remain inherited frozen evidence, not re-estimated in B1.2.
non_blocking_observations: The historical P0 canonical materialization is a single frozen reference value; the design intentionally uses it as a deterministic architecture threshold rather than as a sampled baseline distribution.
P1 and P3 implementation-specific geometry/chunking are still intentionally unresolved but must be frozen before any performance execution.

P3 sidecar should bind an exact raw payload identity in implementation in addition to the canonical tuple-family identity; this is an integrity requirement and does not change the scientific endpoint.
